messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Need a hand. It must stay under 750 m. Keep it to an H or below. Plan for 6 m/s wind. Any ideas?

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Ceiling, not a target. Apogee must stay under 750 m. Motor class H or smaller. Wind is 6 m/s, so that goes in every simulation. Rail, angle and site are not stated: 1.5 m vertical rail, sea level. Landing is not stated, so the 6 m/s gate applies. No diameter, no flight-time window. "Any ideas" means a practical single-stage rocket that clears the gates with margin under the ceiling, not a rocket tuned to kiss 750 m.

2. Feasibility: 750 m is an easy ceiling for H and G motors if the airframe is not tiny. Drag-free speed for 750 m would be sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 750) = 121 m/s, but I want to land well below that, so a mid-size tube and a G-class motor is the conservative choice. Checking two candidates under H.

2. Feasibility: The G64W is 118 N*s and 60.9 N average, 29 mm, mass 0.151 kg, delays 4, 8 and 10 s. That is class G, under the H ceiling. The H128W is 178 N*s and would be the one that crowds 750 m, so I leave it. Drag-free speed at the ceiling is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 750) = 121 m/s. I am not trying to get there.

3. Size: 54 mm cardboard, long enough for a 0.14 m mount. Liftoff guess 0.30 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 60.9 / (0.30 * 9.81) = 20.7. Weight is 0.30 * 9.81 = 2.94 N, rail acceleration (60.9 - 2.94) / 0.30 = 193 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 193 * 1.5) = 24.1 m/s. Chute sizing for about 0.24 kg at 5 m/s: area 2 * 0.24 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 25) = 0.192 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.192 / pi) = 0.50 m. I will fly 0.70 m so the landing stays under 6 m/s in 6 m/s wind. Delay 8 s, ejection deploy.

4. Draft: 54 mm tube 0.55 m, ogive nose, four plywood fins, AeroTech G64W with an 8 s delay, 0.70 m chute. Wind 6 m/s, 1.5 m rail.

4. Check: The simulator gives 739.3 m, under the 750 m ceiling, with 10.7 m to spare. That is not the problem. Margin is 0.69 cal at rail exit and through the burn, under 1.0. Landing is 4.2 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit is 28.1 m/s, thrust-to-weight 15.7. Impulse is 118 N*s, class G, inside H or below. The chute opened at 10.4 s, just after apogee at 10.05 s. Wind in the run is 6 m/s. Drift is 970 m, and the prompt did not cap drift.

5. Fix: The failing value is margin 0.69 cal. One change: larger fins, span 0.13 m and root 0.18 m. Extra fin drag should also pull the apogee further under 750 m, which is the direction the ceiling wants. Motor, tube and chute stay.

4. Check: Apogee moved the right way. The simulator gives 645.4 m, still under 750 m. The fins did not. Margin fell from 0.69 cal to 0.58 cal. The plywood added tail mass and the CP gain did not keep up. Landing is 4.4 m/s. Rail exit is 26.9 m/s, thrust-to-weight 13.8. Ejection is at 10.4 s, after apogee at 9.57 s, and the canopy opens at 8.2 m/s. That is late, but the landing speed still passes.

5. Fix: The failing value is margin 0.58 cal. More fin area made it worse, so this change is nose mass, not fins. One change: 0.06 kg of clay at the top of the tube. The G64W, the 54 mm tube and the chute stay. Altitude should stay under the ceiling.

4. Check: Nose clay fixed the margin without pushing through the ceiling. The simulator gives 635.4 m, under 750 m. Margin is 1.29 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Landing is 4.8 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit is 24.5 m/s, thrust-to-weight 12.2. Impulse is 118 N*s, class G. The chute opens at 10.4 s, 8.3 m/s, after apogee at 9.79 s. Late, but the landing speed passes and the prompt did not cap opening speed. Wind is 6 m/s. Drift is 668 m with no drift limit stated.

5. Fix: nothing left that fails a gate or the ceiling.

6. Uncertainty: Liftoff mass is 0.509 kg, so the 0.06 kg clay is a real fraction of the rocket. Fin plywood is what made the first margin worse. Chute Cd is 0.8. A 10 s delay would open closer to this apogee, but the 8 s delay already lands under 6 m/s and I am not changing a passing flight.

Apogee is 635.4 m, under the 750 m ceiling. Margin is 1.29 cal, landing 4.8 m/s, rail exit 24.5 m/s.
Wind in the flight is 6 m/s. The motor is class G, inside H or below.
